title: Palo Alto Networks in talks to buy AI agent security startup Clutch for $500M
slides: Why is Palo Alto paying $500M for a tiny startup?
Clutch secures AI agents before they reach production.
AI agents can be hijacked to leak data or execute code.
Security teams must now inventory every agent in their stack.
Ask your CISO: who owns agent security today?
thread_text:
1. $500M for a tiny startup?

Palo Alto Networks just dropped half a billion on a company most people have never heard of. The reason: AI agents are entering production faster than security can keep up.

2. Clutch secures AI agents

The startup's platform locks down agents before they go live. It's not about post-breach cleanup — it's about preventing the breach in the first place.

3. Hijacked agents leak data

Attackers can take over AI agents to exfiltrate sensitive information or run malicious code. Your agent could be a backdoor you didn't know you had.

4. Inventory every agent now

Security teams can't protect what they can't see. Start by listing every AI agent in your stack — shadow agents are the new shadow IT.

5. Who owns agent security?

Ask your CISO today. If no one has a clear answer, you've already found your first gap.
